title: Log a failure and rethrow it unchanged

blocks.text: Java 7's *precise rethrow*: when a `catch (Exception e)` block rethrows `e` unchanged, the compiler knows which checked exceptions the `try` block can really throw, so the method declares only those. Write `Audit.runLogged(Step step, List<String> log) throws IOException`:

items: run `step`; if it returns, append `"ok"` to `log`;
if it throws **any** `Exception`, checked or unchecked, append `"failed: " + message` and rethrow that exception. (What happens to an `Error` is not part of this task.)

blocks.text: Keep the `throws` clause to `IOException`. A caller reading the trace of what you rethrow should see where the failure really happened.

cases.says: A step that succeeds logs "ok"; one that throws IOException logs "failed: <message>" and the IOException reaches the caller.
The caught exception is rethrown as the same object, so its original stack trace is kept.
An unchecked exception is logged and rethrown as well, yet the method declares only IOException.
Precise rethrow lets the method declare only IOException, not the Exception its catch clause names.

concepts: Rethrowing an effectively final caught exception declares only what the try block can throw.
Rethrowing the caught exception unchanged keeps its original stack trace.
